text: They took {killer} before the office had the kettle on, and nobody asked me how.
They took {killer} in the end. It cost more of the night than it should have.
The wrong man goes up, and what I never went back for was this: {missed}
A conviction, and a case you could put a thumb through.
The folder goes in the drawer with the others, and the drawer is the end of it.
{detective} filed the report before the sun was properly up, {name} for the noose and the facts to back it. There was time left on the clock and nothing left to do with it.
The file went upstairs clean, {name}'s name at the top and the evidence lined up under it in order. {detective} was home before the milk wagons finished their rounds.
{name} would hang for it, and the report said so plainly, no hour to spare and none wasted either. {detective} signed it and went to find some sleep.
The case closed the way it opened, {name} at the center of it, guilty and proven so with the night's last hour to spare. It was enough.
It took every hour of the night to run {name} to ground, and the report showed it, thin at the edges where the clock had run out on patience. But the case held.
{detective} filed on {name} with the morning already up, tired past arguing, but the facts stood on their own regardless of how long they'd taken to gather.
{name} went to trial, and {detective} closed the file early, sure of it. {missed} never made it into the report, and {killer} read about the verdict same as anybody, over coffee.
It was tidy, and it was wrong. {detective} had it filed with hours to spare, {name} for it, {missed} sitting unasked the whole night through while {killer} went home free.
The report went in on schedule, {name}'s name at the bottom of it. {missed} would have changed everything, but nobody asked, and {killer} never had to answer for it.
{detective} had filed on {name} by the time the case called for it, certain enough. {missed} sat in a drawer somewhere, unlooked-at, and {killer} slept fine.

By the time {detective} filed, worn thin from the hours, {name} looked as good as anybody. {missed} would have said otherwise, if it had come up in time, and {killer} was long past caring whether it did.
It took the whole night and most of the morning, and the report still came out wrong. {missed} sat one question short of being asked, and {killer} walked, and {name} didn't.
{detective} filed early, and the report showed it: half the facts in place and half a guess. The district attorney wouldn't touch it, not on what was there.
There was time left on the clock when {detective} called it, which didn't make the case any less thin for the calling. Nobody would hang on what was filed.
The report went in on time, and it was thin where it needed to be thick, a theory more than a case. {name} walked, for now.
{detective} had a shape for it, right on schedule, but no more than a shape. It wouldn't survive a grand jury, and everybody involved seemed to know it.
By the time the report went in, the night was mostly gone and so was the case's strength. What was left was a theory with the corners rubbed off.
It took past morning to get even this much down, and even this much wouldn't hold up past a magistrate's first question.
{detective} called it early, before the case had a chance to go anywhere. It went into the file unsolved, and stayed there.
There was time left when {detective} gave it up, which didn't change what the file said in the end: nothing closed, nobody named.
The night ran its full course and the case went with it, cold, filed as such, right on schedule.
{detective} had nothing to file but the hours spent, right at the pace the case called for. It went down as unsolved and stayed that way.
The whole night went into it and came out the other side with nothing to show, the case colder for the trying.
By morning there was nothing left to file but the effort. The case went down cold, same as it had started, only later.
